title: Hand3 full profiles transfer partially across sections but short samples do not reliably identify the hand
statement: On disjoint public-practice-training bifolia, a profile averaged equally over six recipe hand3 bifolia is compared with eight botanical CurrierB bifolia, one hand3 Q:2 and seven hand2/5 controls. With six fixed40-word samples per bifolio, the target word-profile rank is2–6 in ZL and2–8 in Takahashi, never first; character and bigram ranks also vary. Full-word descriptive profiles, added after the primary outcomes, agree across both editions: Q:2 is rank3 for raw characters and rank2 for bigrams and words. Full-profile target-minus-control-mean cosine is positive for every feature/edition, but other hands remain closer for at least one bifolio. Thus there is partial whole-profile similarity, with no reliable short-sample or unique cross-section hand identification. All recipe reference units share quire20 and the only herbal hand3 target remains one bifolio.
check: Reproduce every fixed sample and all-feature ranks and margins with the embedded runner and source hashes. To test portability beyond the current one-target geometry, prospectively calibrate sample length and feature power on external multiple-section/multiple-scribe material, then use additional independently attributed target bifolia. Keep full bifolio exclusion, matched lengths and section controls; preserve negative outcomes and use physical units rather than sampling seeds as replication units.

design.estimand: Does the recipe-section hand3 profile place the one botanical hand3 bifolio above botanical hand2/5 controls? Descriptive cross-section transfer; not image paleography or causal hand identification.
design.pages: Use only public practice TRAINING pages in ZL/IT, identical hand/section/Currier metadata, CurrierB, certain P words wholly in acdefghiklmnopqrsty, min40 eligible words per physical Q:B and per edition. Exclude unknown/mixed hand pages. Group all eligible panels of a physical bifolio before sampling. No hidden or all-split lexical outcome.
design.partition: Reference=sectionS hand3, six distinct T bifolia; target=sectionH hand3 Q:2; controls=sectionH hand2 or5. Reference/test physical sets disjoint. Test pages are never in a reference.
design.sampling: Sample exactly40 words without replacement per physical bifolio with seeds13..18, deterministic random.Random per edition/seed/bifolio. All features use the same sampled words. No seed or feature selection after outcomes.
design.metric: Normalize each bifolio feature Counter by Euclidean norm. Average recipe reference vectors equally over physical bifolia, normalize centroid, and compute cosine to each herbal bifolio. Report target rank among all herbal units (midrank ties), target minus mean controls, and target similarity versus leave-one-recipe-bifolio-out cosine. All6 sampling repeats and both editions are repeated measurements.
design.baseline: A classifier seeing only section cannot rank herbal units: all herbal have identical section. Report its tie-midrank (n+1)/2. There is no cross-validated hand-vs-section classifier because sectionS lacks another eligible hand.
design.controls: Six generator backgrounds401..406 using pinned G-self-citation trained only on recipe reference pages, on all eligible layouts. Add separately a positive control replacing10% of sampled words by one fixed marker per annotated hand, same replacement positions across feature types. These controls diagnose procedure sensitivity, not inferential null probabilities. No vocabulary pruning; report zero vectors.
design.support: One target herbal hand3 bifolio, six recipe references in one quire, herbal controls may share quires. No binomial or seed-based significance claims; no hidden-page fact.
design.stop: Report all features, seeds, controls and within-section/cross-section similarity; retain negative transfer. Frozen descriptive design after metadata-only inspection.

plan.timing: Declared after viewing40-word repeated-sample results; not a confirmatory replacement.
plan.reason: Opposite edition signs and varying ranks may reflect finite sampling; describe unsampled normalized profiles.
plan.method: Use all eligible words per physical bifolio in original data only; keep per-bifolio normalized vectors, equal reference-bifolio weighting, fixed3feature sets and same herbal units. No extra scoring threshold or hidden verdict. Unequal total token counts remain a bias/precision limitation.
plan.comparison: The original section-only midrank is4.5 for8 herbal bifolia; report rank and target-control excess, not p.

controls: For exact-word profiles, the10% explicit hand-marker control ranks the target first in all36 background/sample runs per edition, versus3/36 ZL and6/36 Takahashi copying runs. Character/bigram controls are weaker and all ranks are reported, so the negative short-sample results are not evidence that no stable paleographic or lexical signal exists. The fixed marker controls only procedure sensitivity, not realistic effect size. No zero feature vectors occurred.
limitations: These are raw-character and word distributions from transcripts, not visual glyph shapes, stroke order or an independent paleographic reassessment.
One botanical target, six reference bifolia in one quire, shared metadata and paired manuscript transcriptions limit generalization. Sampling seeds are not independent handwriting samples.
All targets have sectionH; a section-only baseline ties all8 at midrank4.5. SectionS has no other eligible annotated hand, so no crossvalidated classifier can independently separate hand and section.

Full-word sensitivity was declared after seeing40-word outcomes; lengths are unequal and the result is descriptive, not a replacement confirmatory outcome. The initial protocol and its hash are retained.

Earlier inventory notes called f115r page-level hand2; the pinned ZL/IT metadata actually leave H unset. This study excludes the mixed/unassigned page. The earlier physical-support bound is unchanged because T:2 was already represented.
No hidden seed/pages were consulted and no hidden fact is submitted.

validation.arithmetic: Analytic checks for unigram/bigram normalization and cosine self-similarity pass. Reference and herbal physical groups are asserted disjoint.

reproduction.usage: Extract the4 files into one folder. From pinned repository root set PYTHONPATH to repository; python path/to/run.py then python path/to/sensitivity.py. Standard library only. Decode compressed_result using base64 then zlib; compare byte sha256.

"""Post-primary descriptive full-word profiles, with independent arithmetic checks."""
import json,math
from pathlib import Path
import run

HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent

def main():
    v=run.vector(['aa','ab'],'chars')
    assert abs(v['a']-3/math.sqrt(10))<1e-12
    assert abs(v['b']-1/math.sqrt(10))<1e-12
    b=run.vector(['aa','ab'],'bigrams')
    assert abs(b['aa']-1/math.sqrt(2))<1e-12
    assert abs(run.cosine(v,v)-1)<1e-12
    pages,meta=run.collect();result={'plan':json.loads((HERE/'sensitivity-plan.json').read_text()),'scores':[]}
    for e,layout in pages.items():
        words=run.groups(layout)
        refs=[b for b in words if meta[b]['section']=='S']
        herbs=[b for b in words if meta[b]['section']=='H']
        target=next(b for b in herbs if meta[b]['hand']=='3')
        for feature in ('chars','bigrams','words'):
            vs={b:run.vector(w,feature) for b,w in words.items()}
            c=run.centroid([vs[b] for b in refs])
            sims={b:run.cosine(vs[b],c) for b in herbs}
            rank=1+sum(x>sims[target]+1e-12 for b,x in sims.items() if b!=target)+.5*sum(abs(x-sims[target])<=1e-12 for b,x in sims.items() if b!=target)
            controls=[x for b,x in sims.items() if b!=target]
            result['scores'].append(dict(edition=e,feature=feature,rank=rank,similarities=sims,
                                         target_minus_mean_control=sims[target]-sum(controls)/len(controls)))
    (HERE/'sensitivity.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps(result['scores'],indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()
